program.dsl:
search synth, synth3d, render

testPattern(pattern: gradient)
  .write(o1)

testPattern(pattern: colorBars)
  .write(o2)

heightmap3d(heightTex: read(o1), tex: read(o2), volumeSize: x32, heightScale: 0.6, baseHeight: 0.1)
  .renderLandscape3d(viewMode: <ortho|perspective>[, filtering: <voxel|isosurface>], rotateX: 0.62, rotateY: 0.5, posY: 12)
  .write(o0)

render(o0)
program.parameterProvenance: upstream renderLandscape3d parity-case.json at 44bc4ed4 (96x80, testPattern gradient/colorBars, volumeSize x32, heightScale 0.6, baseHeight 0.1, rotateX 0.62, rotateY 0.5, posY 12); the nested-call texture form is written as read(o1)/read(o2) because the CPU DSL parser does not accept effect calls as texture arguments; both sides run this exact same text
program.gate: unchanged parity-gate rule: every RGBA byte difference at most 2

cpuSide.entry: CpuRenderer from src/index.js, render(dsl, {width:96, height:80, time:0, seed:1}).toRgba8(); CLI bin/noisemaker-cpu.js render decodes to identical RGBA bytes for all six programs

perspectiveDivergence.note: the (46,75) pixel carries 103 of the 104 total byte difference; CPU renders one extra silhouette voxel facet (0,89,0,255) where the authority shows background (6,11,19,255); the fourth differing byte is a level-1 quantization byte at (37,66)

rootCause.summary: SwiftShader's runtime (uniform-operand) vectorized cos/sin differ from CPU libm f32 rounding; the perspective camera rotation turns a ~4e-3-wide grazing gap into an off-by-one-voxel silhouette difference. Ortho uses no trigonometry and is byte-exact.
rootCause.grazingGeometry: for pixel (46,75) (fragCoord 46.5,4.5): ray-box enter 68.3732235107422, leave 68.37751770019531 (clearance 0.004294); CPU DDA first cell (13,0,31) with atlas density 1
rootCause.atlasAgreement: GPU analyticalGeo texture at (13, 0+31*32) has alpha 1.0 and volumeCache (0,1,0,1) — identical to the CPU atlas, so the divergence is in the ray arithmetic, not the heightfield input

trigMeasurements.method: in-shader debug variants writing fract(v*1024) of the uniforms' vec3 cos/sin into o0 (o0 rgba16f, u8 readback); scalar and literal-vector probes match libm (bytes 105/250/164/238), uniform-operand vec3 probes differ (bytes 114/255/161/236)
trigMeasurements.reconstruction: recomputing inverseRotation with the measured uniform-vec3 trig reproduces the GPU-decoded direction (-0.415508, -0.141065) versus CPU (-0.4154931, -0.1410615) and flips farT.y-nearT.z from +0.0043 to the measured instrumented-shader value -0.00101, so the ray exits before the solid voxel and the authority renders background

rootCause.limits: the debug-variant measurements were taken on instrumented shader compilations; SwiftShader's JIT may schedule the approximation differently per compilation, so the exact operative bits of the uninstrumented program are not recoverable — which is itself the reason the CPU runtime cannot bit-match them
rootCause.classification: same blocker class as GAP-001: the authority backend's undocumented transcendental bit pattern. Emulating one software rasterizer's JIT approximation in the CPU port is not a legitimate parity fix; on other GPUs the grazing pixel could resolve either way
